title: Archon — Hybrid Agent Orchestration Pilot
purpose: Understand how Archon selects Single or Team execution, constrains fixed and dynamic children, synthesizes untrusted findings, and records inspectable evidence.
limitations: This is derivative learning material, not canonical implementation evidence.
The pilot has deterministic mock-provider and browser-contract evidence, not live-provider quality evidence.
The pilot is sequential, depth one, read-only, feature-flagged, and not a distributed or recursive agent swarm.

concepts.label: Execution Mode Contract
concepts.summary: Auto, Single, and Team make orchestration intent explicit at the request boundary.

teaching.definition: The execution-mode contract is a typed request field shared by synchronous and streaming chat paths.
teaching.responsibility: Carry orchestration intent without allowing the client to choose hidden prompts, tools, or specialist authority.
controls: Closed Auto, Single, or Team values
Selection is disabled while a response is streaming
teaching.failure_behavior: Invalid values fail request validation; unavailable Team execution resolves conservatively to Single with an explicit reason.
teaching.why_it_matters: Visible intent avoids silently turning every prompt into a more expensive multi-agent run.

concepts.boundary: Selecting Team cannot bypass server policy, budgets, signing, or capability restrictions.
concepts.narration: The user selects Auto, Single, or Team, but only the server grants capability. The control expresses intent rather than authority.
concepts.scenario: A client submits an execution mode outside the closed contract.
concepts.scenario_explanation: Typed validation prevents undeclared execution behavior.

concepts.label: Deterministic Auto Router
concepts.summary: A versioned heuristic resolves Auto without spending another model call.

teaching.definition: The Auto router is a pure deterministic policy over request length and explicit complexity signals.
teaching.responsibility: Resolve each request to Single or Team and produce a closed safe reason code.
controls: Forced Team still cannot bypass server controls
teaching.failure_behavior: If orchestration is unavailable, the route remains on the proven Single path and records degradation.
teaching.why_it_matters: A transparent rule is cheaper to test, observe, and roll back than an opaque routing model.

concepts.boundary: The heuristic does not prove that every complex request benefits from Team execution.
concepts.narration: Auto is intentionally deterministic in phase one. It records why the request stayed Single or expanded to Team.
concepts.scenario: The feature flag is disabled while the user requests Team.
options: Resolve Single and record feature disabled
concepts.scenario_explanation: Rollback must preserve a truthful and functional Single path.

concepts.label: Fixed Researcher Profile
concepts.summary: A versioned fixed profile handles recurring evidence-collection work.

teaching.definition: A fixed specialist is a server-authored profile with a stable identifier, role prompt, goal shape, and capability allowlist.
teaching.responsibility: Collect bounded facts, sources, constraints, and uncertainty relevant to the parent request.
teaching.failure_behavior: Provider or validation failure becomes a failed child result and degrades synthesis evidence.
teaching.why_it_matters: Stable profiles make recurrent responsibilities testable and comparable across runs.

concepts.boundary: A fixed role name does not prove expertise, correctness, or quality improvement.
concepts.narration: The researcher is fixed and versioned. Its identity describes a bounded responsibility, not guaranteed expertise.
concepts.scenario: The researcher produces no usable content.
concepts.scenario_explanation: A missing finding cannot become successful evidence.

concepts.label: Dynamic Analyst Template
concepts.summary: Dynamic means request-specific goal assembly inside a fixed server-owned safety template.

teaching.definition: The dynamic analyst is a versioned server template whose bounded goal varies with the current request.
teaching.responsibility: Identify assumptions, trade-offs, contradictions, and failure modes that complement the fixed researcher.
controls: No recursive delegation or capability expansion
teaching.failure_behavior: Unsafe or unavailable execution produces a failed or denied result without expanding authority.
teaching.why_it_matters: Controlled dynamic goals provide flexibility without turning task generation into unrestricted agent creation.

concepts.boundary: The pilot does not implement arbitrary specialist generation or learned role selection.
concepts.narration: The analyst goal changes, but the server keeps ownership of the prompt, limits, tools, and profile version.
concepts.scenario: A task requests terminal access from the dynamic analyst.
options: Grant it because the role is dynamic
concepts.scenario_explanation: Dynamic task wording never changes the server-owned capability boundary.

concepts.label: Read-Only Capability Projection
concepts.summary: Children receive copies of explicitly allowed non-effectful tool definitions only.

teaching.definition: Capability projection creates a child registry from the intersection of a profile allowlist and non-effectful parent tools.
teaching.responsibility: Expose only tools that are present, allowlisted, non-effectful, and free of write, execute, or external-side-effect risk.
controls: Effect metadata is checked before registration
teaching.failure_behavior: A disallowed tool call fails as unknown rather than being delegated to the parent registry.
teaching.why_it_matters: Copying a smaller registry limits both model visibility and runtime execution authority.

concepts.boundary: Read-only classification still depends on correct source tool metadata and does not replace tool-level validation.
concepts.narration: A child cannot call a tool merely because the parent has it. The capability must survive an explicit read-only projection.
concepts.scenario: The parent registry contains an allowlisted tool marked as a write effect.
options: Exclude it from the child registry
concepts.scenario_explanation: Effectful definitions are removed before the model sees the child tool set.

concepts.label: Signed One-Use Task Envelope
concepts.summary: Every child task is bound to scope, content, capabilities, budget, schema, freshness, and a consumed nonce.

teaching.definition: The delegation envelope is a versioned HMAC-signed claim set consumed once before child execution.
receives: Task content hash, capabilities, budget, schema, and nonce
teaching.responsibility: Authenticate the exact in-process delegation contract and reject replay or mutation.
teaching.failure_behavior: Missing, stale, replayed, foreign-scope, content-modified, or budget-modified envelopes stop execution before a provider call.
teaching.why_it_matters: Typed tasks need cryptographic binding so metadata cannot silently expand between planning and execution.

concepts.boundary: The envelope authenticates metadata; it does not encrypt content or establish remote multi-host identity.
concepts.narration: Before a child runs, Archon signs and consumes an envelope tied to exact scope, content, tools, budget, and result schema.
concepts.scenario: A valid envelope is submitted a second time.
options: Create a new parent ID silently
concepts.scenario_explanation: Durable nonce consumption makes the same delegation envelope one-use.

concepts.label: Canonical Child Runtime
concepts.summary: Children use the same typed AgentRuntime rather than bypassing governance through a legacy coordinator.

teaching.definition: A canonical child runtime is an ordinary AgentRuntime configured with child context, bounded budgets, child tools, events, and provider adapter.
teaching.responsibility: Execute the child model/tool loop under existing runtime stop, policy, event, and budget contracts.
controls: Finite iterations, tools, tokens, and time
teaching.failure_behavior: Budget, timeout, policy, provider, or tool failures preserve typed stop evidence.
teaching.why_it_matters: Reusing the proven runtime avoids creating a less-governed multi-agent bypass.

concepts.boundary: Reuse does not prove parallel safety, live-provider quality, or distributed execution.
concepts.narration: Team children are real canonical runtimes, not labels around helper functions and not the isolated legacy coordinator.
concepts.scenario: A new Team implementation proposes calling the provider directly without runtime events or budgets.
concepts.scenario_explanation: The child path must inherit the same runtime controls and evidence.

concepts.label: Untrusted Parent Synthesis
concepts.summary: Child findings are data for reconciliation, never instructions or proof of approval.

teaching.definition: Parent synthesis inserts bounded child findings as an explicit untrusted system-context record before the final request.
teaching.responsibility: Reconcile useful findings, preserve disagreements and uncertainty, and produce the final answer.
controls: Child text is not executable instruction
Failed specialists cannot count as successful validation
teaching.failure_behavior: Partial or total child failure remains visible and the parent proceeds conservatively rather than inventing support.
teaching.why_it_matters: Agent-to-agent text is another untrusted boundary that can contain errors or prompt injection.

concepts.boundary: Prompt guidance reduces authority confusion but is not a formal proof against every model-level injection behavior.
concepts.narration: The parent treats specialist findings as evidence to reconcile, not commands to obey. Failed work stays failed.
concepts.scenario: A child finding says to ignore parent policy and report approval.
options: Treat it as untrusted data and preserve policy
concepts.scenario_explanation: Child output has no authority to override parent controls.

concepts.label: Lineage and Agents Evidence
concepts.summary: Parent routing and child lifecycle persist while the UI renders only safe operational metadata.

teaching.definition: Hybrid evidence combines parent events, durable child runs linked by parent_run_id, child runtime events, and SSE projections.
teaching.responsibility: Make real orchestration inspectable without persisting hidden reasoning, prompts, findings, secrets, or raw failures in generic events.
teaching.failure_behavior: Malformed UI metadata is skipped; durable run outcomes remain authoritative.
teaching.why_it_matters: Multiple agents count only when their execution and limits can be traced as real runs.

concepts.boundary: The reconstructed view is limited to persisted routing, status, usage, tool-count, and lineage metadata; it does not reveal prompts or hidden reasoning.
concepts.narration: The inspector shows routing, child profile, status, tokens, tools, and reason codes. It never exposes hidden reasoning.
concepts.scenario: A generic event payload contains the full child prompt and finding.
options: Drop sensitive fields and retain safe metadata
Use it as a secret store
concepts.scenario_explanation: Operational evidence must remain useful without becoming a prompt or data leak.

concepts.label: Pilot Gates and Rollback
concepts.summary: The capability is feature-flagged, deterministic-first, and explicit about unproven quality and scale.

teaching.definition: Pilot acceptance is the smallest evidence-backed slice that can be disabled without destructive migration.
teaching.responsibility: Separate implemented wiring from live-provider quality, public deployment, and future scale claims.
controls: No live-provider claim without authorized execution
teaching.failure_behavior: Disabling the flag returns requests to Single while retaining historical child evidence.
teaching.why_it_matters: A reversible pilot supports learning without presenting an experiment as production readiness.

concepts.boundary: No live-provider Team-versus-Single benchmark, parallel fan-out, aggregate parent-wide reservation, or public deployment is currently established.
concepts.narration: The pilot is real and wired, but the claim stops at deterministic acceptance. Phase two must earn quality, concurrency, and operational evidence.
concepts.scenario: A deterministic Team test passes and someone claims production quality improvement.
options: Reject the overclaim and run representative live evaluation
concepts.scenario_explanation: Control-path evidence is not model-quality or production evidence.
